items.followUp: Write four differences between elements and compounds.

rubric.why: A compound has a fixed composition, unlike a mixture.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a compound has a fixed composition or definite proportion of its elements; a mixture has variable composition.

rubric.why: This distinguishes how the components are held together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that compound components are chemically combined, while mixture components are physically mixed.

rubric.why: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; mixture components retain their properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this contrast.

rubric.why: The means of separating components differ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying compounds are separated by chemical methods and mixtures by physical methods.

modelAnswer: A compound has a fixed composition; a mixture can have a variable composition.
Elements in a compound are chemically combined; substances in a mixture are physically mixed.
A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements; the components of a mixture retain their properties.
A compound can be separated into its elements by chemical methods; the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and write four properties of ionic compounds.

rubric.why: A covalent bond is formed by sharing electron pairs between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining it as a bond formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.

rubric.why: Low melting and boiling points are characteristic of many covalent compounds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally lack mobile charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they generally do not conduct electricity.

rubric.why: Solubility in water and organic solvents is a common distinguishing property.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either correct solubility statement, or for both as in the model answer.

rubric.why: The remaining characteristic in the model answer is that covalent substances are often gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that covalent compounds are generally gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is a chemical bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
They generally do not conduct electricity.
Many are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
They are often gases, liquids, or soft solids at room temperature.

items.followUp: Define evaporation and explain how temperature, humidity, and wind speed affect its rate.

rubric.why: Evaporation takes place at the surface of a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining evaporation as the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface, below its boiling point.

rubric.why: Higher temperature gives liquid particles more kinetic energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that increasing temperature increases the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: A larger exposed surface allows more particles to escape at once.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that increasing surface area increases the rate.

rubric.why: Moving air removes vapour near the liquid surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that greater wind speed increases the rate of evaporation.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface at a temperature below its boiling point.
Increasing the temperature increases the rate of evaporation because more particles gain enough energy to escape.
Increasing the exposed surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
Increasing wind speed increases the rate because moving air carries vapour away from the liquid surface.

items.followUp: State four properties of a true solution and explain how it differs from a colloid.

rubric.why: A colloid is heterogeneous, even though it may appear homogeneous.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a colloid is actually a heterogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles scatter a beam of light, producing the Tyndall effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that colloids scatter light or show the Tyndall effect.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles remain dispersed instead of settling on standing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that colloidal particles do not settle on standing.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles pass through ordinary filter paper.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that colloidal particles pass through ordinary filter paper or cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

modelAnswer: A colloid is actually a heterogeneous mixture, although it may appear homogeneous.
Colloidal particles scatter light and show the Tyndall effect.
The particles do not settle on standing.
The particles pass through ordinary filter paper and cannot be separated by ordinary filtration.

items.followUp: Define a polyatomic molecule and give one example.

rubric.why: A diatomic molecule contains exactly two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a diatomic molecule as one consisting of two atoms.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as O₂, H₂, or N₂.

modelAnswer: A diatomic molecule is a molecule consisting of two atoms.
Example: an oxygen molecule, O₂.

items.followUp: How many particles are present in one mole of a substance? Give the name and value of this number.

rubric.why: Avogadro's number specifies the number of particles in one mole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining Avogadro's number as the number of particles in one mole of a substance.

rubric.why: The numerical value is the key quantitative fact.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the value as approximately 6.02 × 10²³.

modelAnswer: Avogadro's number is the number of particles present in one mole of a substance.
Its value is approximately 6.02 × 10²³.

items.followUp: Define matter and name its three common states.

rubric.why: Matter is defined by having mass and occupying space.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that matter has mass and occupies space.

rubric.why: The textbook identifies three common states of matter.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there are three common states and naming solid, liquid, and gas.

modelAnswer: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.
It has three common states: solid, liquid, and gas.

items.followUp: State three properties of cathode rays.

rubric.why: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying canal rays as positively charged.

rubric.why: Canal rays travel in straight lines.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they travel in straight lines.

modelAnswer: Canal rays consist of positively charged particles.
They travel in straight lines.
They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields; in an electric field, they bend towards the negative plate.
